title: The Dancing Ribbons of Bun Day
markdown:
The sun peeked through the trees, making wiggly gold on the ground. Cora the squirrel, her tail a fluffy question mark, wiggled. "Maple! Maple!" she chirped. "It's bun day! The very best bun day!"

Maple, with fur like warm toast, opened her sleepy eyes. "Bun day?" she whispered.

"Yes! Mr. Waffles the deer made his special berry buns!" Cora twitched her nose. "They smell like sunshine and sweet jam! Yum!" Mr. Waffles lived in a cozy hollow, and his buns were famous.

They scampered down their big oak tree. When they reached Mr. Waffles' sunny spot, they stopped. A long line of friends waited! Fluffy bunnies, busy badgers, and Bartholomew the tortoise, who always took his time. Mr. Waffles, a kind deer, stood by a wobbly table. Little posts with colourful ribbons made a neat line: bright yellow, cheerful red, and pretty green.

Cora and Maple tiptoed to the back. "Look!" whispered Cora. "The ribbons look like happy dancers!"

Mr. Waffles smiled. "They make waiting feel like a party," he said. Just then, a soft breeze whispered, "Whoosh!" It tickled the ribbons, making them sway.

And then, wow! The ribbons began to dance. The yellow ribbon twirled like a happy daffodil. The red ribbon bobbed like a playful ladybug. The green ribbon unfurled like a shy fern.

Everyone forgot about the buns! The rabbit giggled, a tiny sound like rustling leaves. Cora and Maple's noses twitched, their eyes shining. The delicious bun smell faded as they watched the ribbons flutter in shapes like a cloud, a swan, a star. It was a beautiful, silent show.

Suddenly, a soft hoot came from above. It was Gran Ada, their kind owl grandmother. She landed on a branch. "My dears," she hooted gently. "What a lovely display. It seems the air itself wants to play a game."

Cora and Maple pointed. "Look, Gran Ada! The ribbons are playing hide-and-seek!"

Gran Ada chuckled, a warm sound. "Indeed. And sometimes," she said, her eyes twinkling, "it's lovely to stop and watch the world play. The buns will still be here."

Mr. Waffles nodded. "Gran Ada is right," he said. "A moment of beauty is a treat all its own." He picked up two extra-special berry buns. "For Cora and Maple," he winked. "For being such wonderful watchers of the little dances."

Cora and Maple took their buns, their paws sticky with jam. They nibbled happily. The sweet taste was even better after their moment of wonder. They had watched the berry bun ballet, and it was as delightful as any bun.

Walking home with Gran Ada, a sunbeam caught a fallen leaf. It twirled and danced, a tiny ribbon of its own, and Cora and Maple giggled. Bun day had given them more than just yummy buns; it had shown them the world knew how to dance, too.
characters: Cora the squirrel, Maple the squirrel, Gran Ada
